protos_revision_note: reuses the exact pin already validated by ablation 4 (results/perf010a-4), so this Evidence Unit's toolchain/source identity needs no fresh re-derivation; this investigation makes no new claim about that revision's runtime behavior, only about this harness's own measurement discrimination capability
noop_note: docker/protos-perf010a/noop.patch is a literally empty file (0 bytes). It is built through the exact same Dockerfile VARIANT=ablation path as a real ablation (git apply --allow-empty, --allow-dirty, ABLATION_SLICE label) so it exercises identical build/image machinery, but `git apply` on an empty patch changes nothing: the /src tree the noop image compiles is byte-for-byte identical to the baseline image's /src tree. Runtime equivalence is not merely assumed from this: `reference_discrimination`/`smoke_discrimination` additionally assert (via `source_tree_identity_probe`) that the exact source text of every file any prior ablation (1-4) has ever touched is byte-for-byte identical between the baseline and noop images, read from /opt/protos-source, before any timing block runs (NOOP_RUNTIME_PATH_EQUIVALENCE). This deliberately compares source text, not the built protos.jar: this toolchain's Maven build is not byte-reproducible (JAR/ZIP entries embed per-build timestamps), so hashing protos.jar across two separately-built images is build-time noise, not a source-identity proof - an earlier version of this check did that and incorrectly reported FAIL on a genuinely empty patch. The only difference between the two images is harness-local build metadata (ABLATION_SLICE label, /opt/perf010a/ablation-slice.txt, the --allow-empty/--allow-dirty build flags, and non-reproducible build artifact timestamps) - outside the executed Protos runtime path.
jfr_recording_note: the discrimination experiment does not collect per-block JFR structural evidence; the exact-scope/no-op structural contract (source-tree and built-jar identity) is a single per-image static comparison performed once before any block runs, exactly like ablations 3/4's source-derived structural confirmation, not a repeated per-workload JFR profile
cpu_affinity: one physical-core representative from current allowed cpuset
variant_note: the 'ablation' tag slot holds the no-op image for this experiment, reusing the existing baseline/ablation image-build plumbing unmodified; its ABLATION_SLICE label is PERF010A_NOOP_PHASE1_STABLE_IDENTITY, not a real ablation slice
block_design_note: Deterministic AB/BA counterbalanced design, 4 blocks (2 reps of each order), no randomness. Block 'A' order: baseline canonical, baseline control, noop canonical, noop control (matches the existing fixed reference order). Block 'B' order: noop canonical, noop control, baseline canonical, baseline control. Canonical/control pairing within a variant is preserved in both orders; only which variant runs first is counterbalanced. 4 blocks is the smallest design that both (a) separates 'baseline precedes noop' from 'noop precedes baseline' with more than one observation per order, and (b) yields a minimal 4-point descriptive envelope (min/max/median/abs-max) per workload without fabricating an inferential confidence interval from an inadequate sample.
